items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: I have used it on occasion, but I doubled on it in Hamp's band where Milt Rube Buckner wrote things behind vocalists... I was the anchor man.

ctx.x: in Lionel Hampton's band. I have it here now. I run into a guy going into the Army (IN THE 40's) (unintelligible) and he wanted to get rid of the horn and I didn't know what a bass clarinet was. I'd never seen one before in my life. To be so stupid. And he told me he'd sell it to me for $75.00. I said, "$75.00 for this?" He said, "Yeah." I didn't know the value of a -- I'm ignorant about this. Yeah, he's going in the Army and he could -- he isn't going to come out anymore. He's going across-- you know, he…

I had to go to Gladys Hampton and get the money. I didn't have it. That's Lionel Hampton's wife. But I bought it. I've got it right here now in my closet. I have used it on occasion, but I doubled on it in Hamp's band where Milt Rube Buckner wrote things behind vocalists like Rube Blakeley, maybe Dinah Washington on ballads, maybe Madeline Green, maybe Winnie Brown. I'm talking about mostly on vocal tunes or ballads, and you had all clarinets and a bass clarinet, just like you got all the saxophones and a…
